newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - BSkyB shares dip despite profit rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - BSkyB shares dip despite profit rise.

text.p: Shares in British pay television operator BSkyB closed lower on Friday despite the company boosting first quarter pre-tax profit by 31 percent to 66 million pounds ($108.3 million).
BSkyB said it was considering further investment in Germany and would beam its second pay-per-view sports event into Britain later this month.
The satellite broadcaster reported that operating profit rose 20 percent to 79 million pounds in the three months to September 30.
Operating revenues increased to 266 million pounds, a rise of 24 percent on a year earlier. Earnings per share were 3.9 pence, 30 percent up.
BSkyB, in which Rupert Murdoch's News Corp is the leading shareholder with a 40 percent stake, said that total paying subscribers reached 5.65 million, a net increase for the quarter of 146,000.
BSkyB shares closed 10p lower at 568 1/2p, analysts describing subscriber growth as "unexciting".
The shares were also capped by confirmation that News Corp was pressing ahead with plans to raise capital through the sale of $1 billion of preferred securities on its BSkyB stake.
Exact details of the issue are still to be announced but analysts say it shows that Murdoch thinks that the BSkyB share price is fairly high.
However, the message from BSkyB at its annual meeting on Friday was positive.
"The year is off to a strong start and we are looking forward greatly to the months ahead," said deputy managing director David Chance.

BSkyB said in July that it would take a stake of up to 49 percent in DF1, the German digital television venture launched by Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch. BSkyB said on Friday it was considering investments in additional German Pay TV channels.
DF1 has made a slow start but the German pay television market is expected to expand rapidly in coming years.

"Germany is the next important market. We feel there is tremendous upside there," BSkyB chairman Gerry Robinson said. Germany is Europe's biggest television market with 32 million households against 22 million in Britain.
BSkyB said it would show its second pay-per-view event on November 9 when Mike Tyson and Evander Holyfield meet in Las Vegas for the WBA heavyweight boxing crown.
BSkyB successfully experimented with pay-per-view when Tyson fought Briton Frank Bruno in March. More than 660,000 homes paid some 10 pounds to see that fight.

BSkyB plans to introduce digital satellite broadcasting into Britain late next year. Pay-per-view sports events and movies are likely to be one of the prime sources of income from the extra channels provided by digital.
Robinson said BSkyB was hoping that the set-top boxes which decode digital broadcasts could be marketed at 200-300 pounds. But he said that would mean quite a heavy subsidy. ($1=.6096 Pound)
